3. What Buddy does, and what it does not do

Buddy is a remote control for decisions you make. It shows you what your Claude Code sessions are doing, shows you Claude Code’s permission requests and questions, and passes your answer back to Claude Code. From the iPhone, it can also pass a message you write to a Claude Code session, which Buddy for Mac types into that session’s terminal or hands over through Claude Code’s hooks.

  • Buddy never approves anything on its own. If you do not answer, the request goes back to your terminal.
  • Buddy does not review commands, code or messages for safety, security or correctness, and it does not tell you whether to allow them. A command shown on the Mac or the iPhone may be shortened or marked; if you are unsure, answer in the terminal.
  • Choices such as “Always” or approving a plan with automatic edits are your own decisions, and Claude Code acts on them.

4. Your responsibility

You are responsible for every request you allow, every answer you give and every message you send through Buddy, and for what Claude Code and your computer then do, including changes to your code, files, data, accounts and systems. Keep backups and use version control. Keep your Apple Account, Mac and iPhone secure: anyone who can unlock your iPhone may be able to answer requests through Buddy. You are also responsible for following Anthropic’s terms for Claude Code, and the rules of your employer or client when you work on their systems.
